tasks.short: Install python3-gi, gir1.2-atspi-2.0, at-spi2-core; check toolkit-accessibility gsetting
tasks.details: Install python3-gi, gir1.2-atspi-2.0, at-spi2-core; check gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface toolkit-accessibility. python3-gi was already present; gir1.2-atspi-2.0 and at-spi2-core were missing (both needed sudo). toolkit-accessibility was false; set to true via gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface toolkit-accessibility true (per-user dconf, no root needed, but requires restarting apps to take effect). The AT-SPI D-Bus service is activated on demand (org.a11y.Bus → /usr/libexec/at-spi-bus-launcher via at-spi-dbus-bus.service) — nothing to start manually once at-spi2-core is installed. Gotcha: NO_AT_BRIDGE=1 was set in this machine's session environment, which silently disables the GTK ATK→AT-SPI bridge — a plain GTK3 app launched with that var set registers zero AT-SPI children even though accessibility is otherwise on. automonkey must make sure this var is unset (or 0) in the environment it launches/controls apps in. (zenity was unaffected by it in this test, for unclear reasons — don't assume other apps are equally immune.) (From DONE.md, Control actions on Linux (AT-SPI), moved from pywinauto_for_linux.md on 22.10.2026; background notes in docs/linux_atspi.md.)

tasks.group: Linux AT-SPI: Finding windows and controls
tasks.short: get_control dict: control_type -> Atspi.Role mapping
tasks.details: control_type -> role (map pywinauto names: Button -> push button, Edit -> text/entry, Document -> document text,. CheckBox -> check box, ComboBox -> combo box, MenuItem -> menu item, List -> list, ...) — the actual mapping differs from this draft list (see phase 1 findings: get_role_name() strings aren't stable across AT-SPI versions/toolkits). Mapped instead onto the Atspi.Role *enum* (_CONTROL_TYPE_TO_ROLES in atspi_funcs.py), which is the stable identifier - confirmed empirically a GTK push button is Atspi.Role.BUTTON, not PUSH_BUTTON (which exists as a separate enum member, kept in the tuple for other toolkits). Each pywinauto type maps to a tuple of acceptable roles, e.g. "Edit": ("TEXT", "ENTRY", "PASSWORD_TEXT"). Resolved once per get_control call (not per node) so an unknown control_type raises ValueError immediately instead of silently vanishing into a "not found" result. tasks.short: Detect a missing AT-SPI bus / disabled accessibility and say how to enable it
tasks.details: Detect a missing AT-SPI bus / disabled accessibility and print how to enable it. important discovery while implementing this: calling into Atspi (e.g. Atspi.get_desktop(0).get_name()) against a genuinely unreachable bus does not raise a Python exception at all - libatspi's C layer (dbind) prints a fatal dbind-ERROR to stderr and aborts the entire process, confirmed by directly reproducing it (DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS pointed at a nonexistent socket -> the subprocess just died, no traceback, no catchable error). So detection cannot happen by wrapping an Atspi call in try/except - it has to happen *before* anything ever calls into Atspi. Fixed with _atspi_bus_reachable(): a separate dbus-send process (confirmed safe: plain nonzero exit + stderr message, no abort) queries org.a11y.Bus.GetAddress with a 3s timeout; _atspi() runs this once per process (cached in _env_checked, re-tried if it previously failed) before ever handing out the Atspi module, raising a clear ConnectionError if the bus is down. Confirmed: merely from gi.repository import Atspi (without calling anything) is safe even with a dead bus - only the bus check's placement, not the import itself, mattered. Also added _check_accessibility_enabled(): a gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface toolkit-accessibility check (warn-only, same one-time cache) that tells the user to enable it and restart apps if it's false. (From DONE.md, Control actions on Linux (AT-SPI), moved from pywinauto_for_linux.md on 22.10.2026; background notes in docs/linux_atspi.md.)

tasks.short: Enable the commented-out pytest step in python-package.yml
tasks.details: Enable the commented-out pytest step in .github/workflows/python-package.yml. both done together: added an apt-get step (python3-gi gir1.2-atspi-2.0 at-spi2-core xvfb dbus-daemon gnome-calculator gnome-text-editor - dbus-daemon provides dbus-run-session on this box, confirmed via dpkg -S), uncommented the pytest step and wrapped it in xvfb-run -a dbus-run-session -- pytest, and set AUTOMONKEY_ATSPI_INTEGRATION=1 so CI actually exercises the integration tests rather than just skipping them. Known, documented tradeoff, not silently glossed over: python3-gi installs PyGObject for Ubuntu's own system python3, not for whichever interpreter actions/setup-python puts on PATH for a given matrix entry (the workflow's existing matrix is Python 3.8/3.9/3.10, set long before this AT-SPI work and not touched here - that's a separate, pre-existing staleness issue, not something this phase should quietly take on). Wired by appending /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages to sys.path in-process around pytest.main() - the trick used throughout this implementation to let a different interpreter see system-installed gi, but as a plain PYTHONPATH it pre-empted this job's own installed packages and broke pytest's plugin loading, hence the in-process append after pytest's own startup. This only lines up cleanly when a matrix entry's Python version matches the runner's system python3 ABI - 3.8/3.9/3.10 against ubuntu-latest's 3.12 system python does not, so on CI these two tests skip. Fixed 2026-10-16: they used to *fail* there (a plain ImportError from gi), which turned the matrix red on every version - and once the publish job was gated on the matrix, that would have blocked every release over an environment quirk unrelated to this repo's code. tests/test_atspi_integration.py now checks the bindings itself (_atspi_bindings_available(), which catches the half-working import gi -> from . import _gi failure) and skips, so the file keeps its "always safe to collect/run" contract. Verified by reproducing that exact broken-gi shape locally: a fake gi package that raises on from . import _gi -> binding check False and the file collects and skips cleanly; a working fake -> binding check True. The commands in section 5 still run these tests for real on a box whose python3 has python3-gi. Could not be verified by actually running GitHub Actions from here - YAML syntax was validated with a local parse, and the underlying command pattern (xvfb-run / fakeroot X + dbus-run-session for a private AT-SPI bus) is the standard approach for headless accessibility testing, but the workflow itself is unverified end-to-end. (From DONE.md, Control actions on Linux (AT-SPI), moved from pywinauto_for_linux.md on 22.10.2026; background notes in docs/linux_atspi.md.)

tasks.short: setup.py: document that PyGObject comes from the distro; pywinauto stays Windows-only
tasks.details: setup.py: add a linux extra (or document that PyGObject comes from the distro); keep pywinauto Windows-only. chose document, not a pip extra: PyGObject genuinely isn't a reliable pip install (needs system build deps - cairo, gobject-introspection headers, pkg-config - that aren't guaranteed present, confirmed in this very project by how we actually got it working: apt-get install python3-gi ..., never pip). A fake extras_require={'linux': [...]} would either be empty (useless) or silently fail to build for most users, worse than no extra at all. Documented instead via a module docstring in setup.py plus Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows / :: POSIX :: Linux classifiers. pywinauto was already Windows-only (requirements.txt's sys_platform == 'win32' marker, pre-existing, untouched). (From DONE.md, Control actions on Linux (AT-SPI), moved from pywinauto_for_linux.md on 22.10.2026; background notes in docs/linux_atspi.md.)

tasks.details: Final review: running the integration tests for real. gnome-calculator and gnome-text-editor were installed after the Tests section, so tests/test_atspi_integration.py ran for real. Both tests first failed and exposed three real issues, all fixed: start_app kept the caller's stdout open (now DEVNULL + start_new_session=True); rapid do_action calls outrun the app (the test sleeps between clicks, the library does not); Component.grab_focus() fails app-wide on gnome-text-editor (GTK4), so _grab_focus falls back to a mouse click on the control's extents. Also confirmed again the Wayland keyboard-injection limit, and _stop() got a SIGKILL fallback. Verified 2026-10-13 on real gnome-calculator/gnome-text-editor (GDK_BACKEND=x11): both integration tests pass, full suite 38 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed, no leftover GUI processes. tasks.short: Fill depends_on in every open task that waits for another task
tasks.details: New optional field of tasklist.json: "depends_on": an array with the ids (with the repository prefix, e.g. "AutoMonkey-N27") of the tasks that must be done first. The Tasklist tab shows it in the details of a task. Go through every open (todo) task, read its details (e.g. "waits for H2", "continues P2.3", "after N5") and the order of the list, and set depends_on where a task really needs another one (including human tasks it waits for). Use `wb tasklist-edit <id> --depends_on <id1,id2> --repo AutoMonkey` or edit the file; keep the ids that exist in this list (the tasklist-check hook rejects unknown ones). Do not invent dependencies. Check with node ~/.claude/hooks/tasklist-check.js tasklist.json.
